 -4-  MFA No. 1825/2021  C/W MFA No. 5325/2020  JUDGMENT Challenging the award in MVC No.877/2018 on the file of I-Additional Senior Civil Judge & CJM and MACT, Mangaluru the Insurer has preferred MFA No.1825/2021 and the claimants have preferred MFA No.5325/2020.
2.
For the purpose of convenience the parties will be referred to henceforth according to the ranks assigned to them before the Tribunal.
3. Claimant No.1 is the wife, claimant No.2 is the son and claimant Nos.3 and 4 the married daughters of deceased M.Devappa Shetty.

On 10.01.2018 at 4.00 p.m. when M.Devappa Shetty was crossing the road near A.B Shetty Circle within the jurisdiction of Mangalore West Traffic Police station, the auto-rickshaw bearing registration No.KA.19-AA-3047 hit him and caused the accident.
Due to the injuries suffered in the accident, Devappa Shetty was shifted to Government Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore where he was declared brought dead.

4. Regarding the accident Neeladhar Shetty/PW.2 filed complaint as per Ex.P2 alleging that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of the driver of the auto-rickshaw bearing registration No.KA.19-AA-3047.
Based on such complaint, Mangalore Traffic Police registered FIR as per Ex.P1 against the driver of the said auto- rickshaw.
On conducting the investigation charge sheet as per Ex.P10 was filed against the driver of the auto-rickshaw for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 304A IPC.
At the relevant time respondent Nos.1 and 2 were respectively the registered owner and Insurer of the aforesaid auto-rickshaw.
5. Claimants filed MVC No.877/2018 contending that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence of the driver of the auto-rickshaw.
They further contended that the deceased Devappa Shetty was earning huge income from his liquor business and agriculture and they were all dependents on his income.
Thus they claimed compensation of Rs.1,35,00,000/-(Rupees one crore thirty-five lakhs only) from the respondents.
6. Respondent No.1 did not contest the petition.

Respondent No.2 contested the petition denying the occurrence of the accident due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the auto-rickshaw,
age, occupation, income of the deceased and its liability to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: In support of their case, claimants examined claimant No.1 as PW.1 and complainant as PW.2.
On their behalf Exs.
P1 to 22 were marked.
No oral evidence was adduced on behalf of respondents.
On behalf of respondent No.2 Exs.R.1 to R6 were marked.

8. The Tribunal on hearing the parties by the impugned award relying on Exs.P1 to P10 held that the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the auto-rickshaw bearing registration No.KA.19-AA-3047.
The Tribunal further held that the claimants were the dependents of the deceased.

Relying on Exs.P19 to 21 the Income Tax Returns of the deceased the Tribunal considered his annual income at Rs.22,16,426/-, deducted 1/3rd towards his personal expenses,
applied 5 multiplier and awarded compensation of Rs.73,88,040/- on the head of loss of dependency.

The Tribunal in all awarded compensation of Rs.75,08,040/- on different heads as per the table below:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of dependency 73,88,040/-
 2. Loss of Consortium 40,000/-
 3. Loss of Love and Affection 50,000/-
 4. Loss of Funeral Expenses 15,000/-
 5. Loss of Estate 15,000/-
 Total 75,08,040/-

Submissions of Sri Seetha Rama Rao B.C, learned Counsel for the Insurer:
9.
As per the claimants' own record, the deceased was aged 71 years.
Claimant Nos.2 to 4 were the major son and major married daughters of the deceased.
PW.1 in her evidence has unequivocally admitted that during the life time of the victim himself and claimant No.2 were running liquor business.
Her admission further shows that after the death of Devappa Shetty claimant No.2 is running the business.
Therefore, there was no loss of dependency at all.
Neither claimant No.2 was examined nor his Income Tax Returns of the subsequent year were produced to show that there was reduction in the business income.
Regarding the alleged agricultural income absolutely no material was produced.
Out of the income of the deceased  has to be deducted for his personal expenses.
Under the circumstances, the Tribunal committed error in awarding compensation on the head of loss of dependency.

Submissions of Sri H.Malatesh, learned Counsel for the claimants:
10.
The Income Tax Returns Exs.P19 to 21 show that the deceased by managerial skill was deriving income at Rs.30,73,410/- that included the agricultural income also.
After the death of the victim there was reduction in the income which is deposed by PW.1.
Therefore, awarding compensation on the head of loss of dependency does not warrant interference of this Court.
The compensation awarded on the conventional heads and consortium is on the lower side.

sentences.text: Having regard to the submissions of both side and on perusing the records, the question that arise for consideration is "Whether the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just one?"
Analysis 12.
So far as the relationship of the parties, occurrence of the accident and cause of death there is no dispute.
The owner of the vehicle himself did not challenge either before the Tribunal or before this Court the occurrence of the accident due to actionable negligence of the driver of the auto-rickshaw.
Therefore that finding of the Tribunal has attained finality.
13. As per Ex.P12 the passport of the deceased, his date of birth was 25.05.1947.
Therefore, as on the date of his death he was aged 71 years.
There is no dispute that the deceased was running Prashanth Wines and his Income Tax Returns Exs.P19 to 21 were not seriously disputed.
The relevant Income Tax Returns was Ex.P21 which was for assessment year of 2017-18 submitted on 30.10.2017.
As per the said record the total income of the deceased was Rs.32,27,181/-.
The Net Tax payable on the same was Rs.8,56,984/-.

Therefore net income was Rs.23,70,199/-.
14.

Though the claimants contended that they were all dependent on the income of the deceased,
their own claim petition shows that claimant No.2 the son was aged 44 years and daughters/claimant Nos.3 and 4 were aged 46 and 40 years.
Claimant Nos.3 and 4 were married daughters.
The claim petition shows that they were residing in the houses of their respective husband separately from their parents.

Despite respondent No.2 disputing their dependency,
- 10 - claimant Nos.2 to 4 did not enter the witness box to assert that they were dependent on the income of the deceased.
15. PW.1 the mother in her cross-examination admitted that the Wine shop was being run by her husband and her son.
She further admitted that after the death of her husband her son is looking after the said business and wine shop licence was not cancelled.
She further admitted that the licence was transferred in the name of the second claimant.
She also admitted that after the death of her husband also they were running the business as earlier.

16. Though PW.1 claimed that the income of the business was reduced, to substantiate the said contention the Income Tax Returns of the business of claimant No.2 subsequent to the death of Devappa shetty were not produced.
Therefore the Tribunal committed error in holding that claimant Nos.2 to 4 were dependent on the deceased.
Under the circumstances only claimant No.1 becomes the dependent of the deceased.

In that event as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1 half of the income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal and living AIR 2009 SC 3104 - 11 - United India Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Shashikala on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89021340/
6 expenses which comes to Rs.11,85,099/- (23,70,199  2) rounded to Rs.11,85,100/-.

sentences.text: 17. Since there was no loss of income to the claimants on the death of the deceased, as per the judgment of this Court in A Manavalagan Vs A Krishnamurthy and others2 the claimants will be entitled to compensation only on the head of loss of estate.

entities.text: A Manavalagan Vs A Krishnamurthy and others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the claimants relying on the judgment in K Ramya and others Vs National Insurance Company Ltd., and others3 tried to contend that mere transfer of the business venture of the deceased to his children will not reduce the loss of income or the dependency.

entities.text: K Ramya and others Vs National Insurance Company Ltd., and others3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reading of the said judgment shows that in that case the deceased was aged 31 years and his surviving children were all minors.
Therefore, the said judgment cannot be justifiably applied for the facts of the present case and the Judgment in A Manavalagan's case has to be applied.
18. As per the judgment in A Manavalagan's case, the claimants are entitled to 25% of the income of the deceased on the head of loss of estate.
The applicable multiplier is 5.
Therefore the compensation payable on the head of loss of estate is (2,96,275/- x 5) Rs.14,81,375/-.

As per the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi4 and Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Nanu Ram5 cases, each of the claimants is entitled to compensation on the head of consortium at the rate of 40,000/- with an escalation at 10%.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Ltd. v. Nanu Ram5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the compensation payable on the head of consortium comes to Rs.1,76,000/-.

19. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi's case referred to supra the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on the head of funeral expenses and transportation charges with the escalation of 10% which comes to Rs.16,500/-.

Therefore, the just compensation payable is as follows:
 Sl. Particulars Compensation  No. awarded in Rs.
 1. Loss of estate 14,81,375/-
 2. Loss of Consortium 1,76,000/-
 3. Loss of Funeral Expenses and 16,500/-
 transportation charges

sentences.text: In the light of the above observations, both the appeals deserve to be allowed in part.

Hence the following:
ORDER
The appeals are partly allowed.

The impugned order is modified as follows:
a) The claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.16,73,875/- with interest thereon at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the realisation.
b) Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the said compensation to the claimants.
c) Respondent No.2/Insurer is liable to pay the said compensation to the claimants.

d) The compensation amount is apportioned in the ratio of 70% to claimant No.1 and 10% each to claimant Nos.2 to 4.
e) Registry shall transmit the award amount with proportionate accrued interest and TCRs to the Tribunal forthwith.
The remaining amount in deposit shall be refunded to the appellant-Insurer.
